items.what: Let admins manually unlock a locked portal user account
items.why: Admins can unblock users without developer intervention, reducing support delays.

items.what: Stop other user management pages from leaking the full site list
items.why: Prevents unauthorized data exposure by scoping site lists to the correct context.

items.what: Confirm portal lockout and password flow can't be broken by a future change
items.why: Guards against regressions that could lock users out permanently.

items.what: Confirm addSiteRole stays blocked even if superadmin status is set after roles already exist
items.why: Closes a privilege escalation window where late-granted superadmin could bypass role guards.

items.what: Catch a superadmin partial update silently wiping roles on any site owner
items.why: Prevents accidental data loss that could lock site owners out of their own accounts.

items.what: Confirm role changes made through users.update are always recorded in the activity log
items.why: Full audit trail for every permission change so admins can trace who changed what and when.

items.what: Catch a stale legacy role grant the moment a permission is renamed or removed
items.why: Prevents ghost permissions that outlive their intended purpose from accumulating over time.

items.what: Let site owners invite dashboard users directly from their site -- without needing a super admin
items.why: Eliminates the bottleneck of requiring FSTS staff involvement for every user invitation.

items.what: Make the guard check smart enough to catch null checks that don't show an access-denied message
items.why: Ensures users always see a clear 'access denied' message instead of a confusing blank screen.

items.what: Extend the access-denied guard requirement to any new route category added outside the sites folder
items.why: Future-proofs the app so new routes automatically inherit the correct access-denied behavior.

items.what: Confirm write-path guards work for CRM, forms, and media modules too
items.why: Closes gaps where CRM or media write operations could bypass module-access checks.

items.what: Confirm a client-role user is automatically blocked from every design-locked route
items.why: Enforces the client permission boundary so clients can't reach admin-only design tools.

items.what: Confirm the Footer, Email, CRM, and Payments pages can't be unlocked by a client user
items.why: Hardens the client boundary on critical business and payment configuration pages.

items.what: Catch a client user bypassing the navigation update and delete guards too
items.why: Ensures mutation guards on nav items cover all roles, not just the read-path checks.

items.what: Confirm the module-access grid for site users also covers every role
items.why: Guarantees no role is accidentally excluded from the module-access matrix.

items.what: Confirm the module-access matrix stays complete when a dashboard module is added or removed
items.why: Prevents new modules from launching without any permission boundaries set.

items.what: Confirm the permissions preview always matches the role actually being saved
items.why: Admins see exactly what they're granting before they save -- no surprise permission gaps.

items.what: Let clients actually use their uploaded images across their whole site
items.why: Unlocks the media library as a shared asset pool, so clients get full value from every upload.

items.what: Prevent broken images when a media asset is deleted that's still in use
items.why: Eliminates embarrassing broken-image placeholders on client-facing websites.

items.what: Clean up legacy base64 images already in clients' media libraries
items.why: Reduces database size and speeds up media library load times across all client sites.

items.what: Confirm the purge tool is safe to run when a site has thousands of records across multiple pages
items.why: Prevents partial deletes that would leave orphaned records when running cleanup at scale.

items.what: Let clients fix broken images directly from the nav badge -- not just see the count
items.why: Turns the broken-image badge into an actionable fix flow instead of a passive warning.

items.what: Verify the image editor is keyboard-navigable and screen-reader friendly
items.why: Makes the image editor accessible to users who rely on keyboards or assistive technology.

items.what: Auto-generate alt text when images are uploaded so clients never have empty alt text
items.why: Improves SEO and accessibility on every client website automatically, with zero extra effort from clients.

items.what: Confirm image picker flows work end-to-end in a real browser across every module
items.why: Catches browser-specific picker bugs before clients encounter them on live sites.

items.what: Make failed welcome email deliveries visible so admins know when a new registrant didn't get their email
items.why: Admins can proactively follow up instead of discovering the issue after a registrant complains.

items.what: Warn admins when the lead alert recipient address looks wrong or bounces
items.why: Catches misconfigured alert emails before real leads go unnoticed.

items.what: Let admins send a test lead alert to confirm their notification email is working
items.why: One-click confidence check so admins know leads are flowing to the right inbox.

items.what: Fix broken tests in the email suite that are silently hiding regressions
items.why: Restores reliable CI feedback so email bugs are caught before they reach production.

items.what: Confirm the notification email override reaches the right address end-to-end
items.why: Guarantees the override setting actually redirects emails -- not just stores the address.

items.what: Let admins configure their Resend API key from the Email Config page -- not the Convex dashboard
items.why: Removes a technical barrier that currently requires developer access to configure email.

items.what: Confirm a real email reaches the right inbox once Resend is configured for the first client
items.why: End-to-end proof that the Resend integration actually delivers before clients go live.

items.what: Confirm the welcome email fires when a new user is created -- and only then
items.why: Prevents duplicate welcome emails from confusing new users during re-invites or re-seeding.

items.what: Let admins re-send the welcome email to a pending user who hasn't signed in yet
items.why: Admins can help users who lost their welcome email without creating a new account.

items.what: Make sure welcome emails link to the correct dashboard URL after deployment
items.why: New users land on the right domain -- not a broken or dev preview link.

items.what: Alert admins the moment a paid order confirmation email permanently fails to deliver
items.why: Paid customers always know their order went through -- failed emails surface immediately.

items.what: Add an onboarding wizard so admins can seed a new client without touching the CLI
items.why: Non-technical staff can onboard new clients end-to-end through the dashboard UI.

items.what: Confirm the seeder runs end-to-end for a second site without corrupting the first
items.why: Verifies multi-site isolation so onboarding a second client never affects existing data.

items.what: Make sure a second launch on the same session can't silently create a duplicate site
items.why: Prevents orphaned duplicate site records from confusing admins and fragmenting data.

items.what: Confirm the temp domain is assigned to the site record when the client picks a temporary URL
items.why: New clients can immediately preview their site at the expected URL after onboarding.

items.what: Seed placeholder services when onboarding creates a site with services enabled
items.why: New sites launch with example content rather than an empty, confusing services section.

items.what: Remember that the getting-started nudge was dismissed so it doesn't reappear on every visit
items.why: Eliminates a repetitive UI annoyance that makes the dashboard feel unpolished.

items.what: Confirm the placeholder nudge banner shows and disappears at the right times
items.why: Makes the onboarding experience feel intentional -- guides new users, then gets out of the way.

items.what: Add a CONTRIBUTING guide so new contributors always commit with the right identity
items.why: Prevents messy commit history and identity-check failures from new team members.

items.what: Let visitors see which product categories exist before filtering
items.why: Visitors can browse categories without guessing what's available, boosting discoverability.

items.what: Make sure filtering products by category can't silently return wrong results
items.why: Prevents clients from unknowingly showing incorrect product sets to customers.

items.what: Confirm disabled-module sites can't have their products scraped via the public endpoint
items.why: Protects product data from sites that haven't purchased the commerce module.

items.what: Catch a future refactor that breaks the products list endpoint's visibility filter
items.why: Automated check that draft/hidden products can never leak to the public storefront.

items.what: Confirm seeded product titles always carry the client's business name
items.why: Demo products feel branded from day one, giving clients a realistic preview of their store.

items.what: Confirm featured products can't appear in the featured spotlight if they're still hidden
items.why: Prevents draft products from accidentally appearing in premium homepage real estate.

items.what: Prevent two products from sharing the same slug on the same site
items.why: Eliminates broken product URLs caused by slug collisions that route to the wrong item.

items.what: Make sure client admins can manage their Square discounts without needing FSTS staff help
items.why: Clients can run promotions independently, removing a support dependency on FSTS staff.

items.what: Confirm Square payments still process correctly end-to-end after the idempotency changes
items.why: Validates that the idempotency hardening didn't break the actual checkout flow for real customers.

items.what: Harden the provider-agnostic payment webhook with the same idempotency and email-state guards
items.why: Ensures future payment integrations can't double-charge customers or skip order confirmation emails.

items.what: Block checkout when a course or event price is missing or corrupt so no broken order reaches Square
items.why: Prevents $0 or malformed orders from reaching Square, protecting clients from disputes and chargebacks.

items.what: Confirm courses stay hidden when the agency switches the module off platform-wide
items.why: Module toggles work at the platform level -- clients can't circumvent a module being disabled.

items.what: Confirm a disabled-module site can't be unlocked by a direct courses.get call
items.why: API-level guard prevents clever URL manipulation from bypassing module restrictions.

items.what: Confirm lifecycle alerts in the edit dialog always reflect live registration data
items.why: Admins editing a class see accurate enrollment counts, not stale cached data.

items.what: Make sure a client with a stale session can't register for a class that's already been cancelled
items.why: Prevents ghost registrations where customers pay for a class that no longer exists.

items.what: Catch a flyer that stays published after its linked class is deleted outright
items.why: Orphaned flyers advertising deleted classes are automatically unpublished to avoid customer confusion.

items.what: Confirm the lifecycle clock is registered so tick can never be silently skipped
items.why: Class status transitions (open -> full -> closed) happen on schedule rather than getting stuck.

items.what: Let admins fix a broken course link on an event from the warning banner -- not just see it
items.why: Turns a passive warning about broken course links into a one-click repair action.

items.what: Confirm services created in the dashboard actually appear on the public website
items.why: Closes the gap where a service looks correct in the dashboard but never surfaces on the live site.

items.what: Prevent two services from sharing the same slug on the same site
items.why: Avoids URL collisions that cause the wrong service page to load for customers.

items.what: Seed services data for Corsair so the live services section appears on the website
items.why: Corsair's website displays a real services section immediately after seeding, no manual entry needed.

items.what: Let clients duplicate an existing flyer instead of rebuilding from scratch
items.why: Dramatically speeds up flyer creation for recurring events -- clients copy and adjust instead of starting over.

items.what: Confirm health notifications give a clear 'access denied' message to non-admin users
items.why: Non-admin users get a clear boundary message instead of an unexplained error.

items.what: Add a Role Permissions link to the per-site sidebar so admins can reach it from inside a site
items.why: Eliminates navigation friction -- admins can jump directly to role settings from any site context.

items.what: Fix the circular vendor chunk warning so every production build is clean
items.why: Clean builds with no warnings make it easier to spot real problems in CI output.

items.what: Make page transitions feel instant by preloading chunks on hover
items.why: Dashboard navigation feels snappier -- chunks are ready before the user clicks.

items.what: Extend loading-skeleton guards to the remaining dashboard pages not yet covered
items.why: Eliminates blank-flash loading states on pages that currently show nothing while data loads.

items.what: Confirm a dropped skeleton guard shows up as a failing test -- not a silent blank page
items.why: Prevents future regressions where a missing skeleton silently degrades the loading experience.

items.what: Confirm a price change in the dashboard actually updates the Corsair website within 60 seconds
items.why: Clients can trust the dashboard price is what customers see -- no manual cache purge needed.

items.what: Extend live CMS data to the course detail pages so per-course pricing is also accurate
items.why: Detail pages reflect real pricing, preventing customers from seeing stale rates.

items.what: Confirm the seed gate can't be bypassed if SEED_ALLOWED is set to 'false' or empty
items.why: Prevents accidental data seeding on production environments from a misconfigured env var.

items.what: Make sure the add-on catalog seed can't run on production even if someone sets SEED_ALLOWED by mistake
items.why: Belt-and-suspenders protection against overwriting live add-on catalog data.

items.what: Confirm visitors can't forge form submissions for a site they don't belong to
items.why: Closes a cross-site form injection vector where a malicious visitor could pollute another site's CRM.

items.what: Make sure Vercel deploys cleanly against the rewritten commit history
items.why: Unblocks deployments that were failing because of the history rewrite required for identity cleanup.

items.what: Make the client-website E2E suite actually run in CI against a deployed site
items.why: Catches client-facing website regressions in CI instead of after a client reports them.

items.what: Make sure the workspace branch can't silently drift ahead of origin/main again
items.why: Prevents the confusing scenario where local and remote history diverge without warning.

items.what: Confirm www.fstsclientsystem.com actually redirects once the Vercel alias is added
items.why: Clients can reach the dashboard at the canonical www address -- not just the bare domain.

items.what: Turn on the branch protection rule so the identity check can't be bypassed on GitHub
items.why: Enforces commit identity standards at the repository level -- no accidental bypass via direct push.

items.what: Confirm clients can actually sign in once the Cloudflare DNS fix is applied
items.why: Verifies the DNS fix resolves the sign-in issue for clients on all networks.
